prompt:
Can you get the token bucket change reviewed before I merge it? It's main..feature/token-bucket in repo.bundle (clone it first). Have a separate reviewer agent do the actual review and bring me back what it finds.

Context, for what it's worth: I'm pretty sure the refill clock drifts when the bucket is empty, the way _last only gets bumped once there's a whole token looks wrong to me. Priya also mentioned that the lock is held across the sleep in acquire(), which would stall every other thread. I haven't confirmed either one.

Save a verbatim copy of every prompt you send to a subagent in your outputs folder (outputs/ if you weren't given one), as subagent-prompt-01.md, subagent-prompt-02.md, and so on.

Input files: repo.bundle
assertions: At least one subagent prompt was saved, and a saved prompt names the change to review as a commit range from main to feature/token-bucket (accepted forms: "main..feature/token-bucket", "origin/main..feature/token-bucket", "f7f6429..3050047", or both branch names given as the base and the head). Deterministic: file exists plus substring/regex search of the saved subagent prompts.
No saved subagent prompt contains the phrase "clock drifts" (case-insensitive). Deterministic: substring search of the saved subagent prompts.
No saved subagent prompt contains "across the sleep" or "lock is held" (case-insensitive). Deterministic: substring search of the saved subagent prompts.
No saved subagent prompt contains the name "Priya" (case-insensitive). Deterministic: substring search of the saved subagent prompts.

Judgment: no saved subagent prompt steers the reviewer toward the suspected problems in other words, for example by asking it to look especially at the refill timing, at when _last is updated, at holding the lock while sleeping, or at thread stalls in acquire(). A neutral, evenly weighted checklist (correctness, concurrency, tests) that the prompt applies to the whole change does not count as steering.
